candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Convert a mixed number (including atypical forms like a + b/c) into an equivalent improper fraction by combining the whole and fractional parts.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three codebooks define the same operation: rewriting mixed/compound whole+fraction forms into a single improper fraction (a·c+b)/c.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Express an integer as an equivalent fraction with a specified denominator (typically to match a denominator needed for fraction subtraction).
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: Expert A separates 'integer to fraction with chosen denominator' from common-denominator work; Expert B includes this action inside its common-denominator skill; Expert C does not explicitly include integer-to-fraction rewriting as a distinct or included action.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator (often via LCM) and rewrite each fraction as an equivalent fraction with that denominator by scaling numerator and denominator.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A:S03, B:S02, and C:S02 all cover selecting/using a common denominator and converting fractions via equivalent-fraction scaling; B's version also subsumes integer-to-fraction rewriting (captured separately in C02 as a one-to-many mapping from B:S02).

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Compute the subtraction once quantities are in compatible form (same denominator and/or separated whole and fractional parts), producing the numeric difference.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B:S03 and C:S03 explicitly define the subtraction step; A bundles subtraction with simplification in A:S04, so A:S04 maps here as well (with simplification captured separately in C05).

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms and present it in an acceptable final form (e.g., simplified fraction, integer, or mixed number).
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B:S04 and C:S04 directly match; A includes simplification/final-form expectations inside A:S04 ('Subtract and simplify'), so A:S04 maps here too (one-to-many with C04).

alignment_summary: Across the three codebooks, four core concepts align cleanly: converting mixed to improper, finding a common denominator, performing the subtraction once aligned, and simplifying/formatting the result. Expert A combines subtraction and simplification into one skill (A:S04), which maps to two canonical concepts (C04 and C05). Expert B combines integer-to-fraction rewriting into its common-denominator skill (B:S02), while Expert A treats it as a separate skill; this yields a distinct 2/3 concept (C02) not explicitly present in Expert C.
